I have been farming these 8.5 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. I never went to school, but I know every ridge and hollow of my land better than any book. My children work in the city part of the year, so most days it is just me and my old man out here, and our bones are not what they used to be. Still, we manage. We have our own well, which is a blessing — when the sky forgets to rain, we can pump water, though the electricity bill stings.

This year I will keep 5 mu in my wheat-maize rotation, same as always. The wheat went in last October — I bought improved seeds from the shop, about 30 jin per mu, the same kind my neighbor across the road planted. Before sowing I already spread two bags of compound fertilizer on that plot. Now that the wheat is waking up, I will run the rotary tiller through it lightly to break the crust, and when it starts jointing I will topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. I will irrigate three times: once now to wake it up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice for weeds and the bugs that always come when it warms up. If we do not get a late frost, I should harvest about 950 jin per mu.

My sunflower goes on the other 3.5 mu. I had the rotary tiller go over that ground last month to smooth it out. I bought hybrid sunflower seeds — one and a half small packages per mu. I spread about two bags of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing. Sunflower is tough and does not need as much water, so I will irrigate twice, and spray twice to keep the weeds down. Last year the birds got some, but if I am lucky I will get around 700 jin of seeds per mu, and the buyer at the market pays good money for clean sunflower seeds.

After we cut the wheat in early June, there is no time to plough — the season is too short. We plant the maize straight into the wheat stubble, no-tillage. I use hybrid maize seeds, the big yellow kernel type, one package per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the planting holes, about a bag and a half per mu, and irrigate twice in the summer if the rains do not come. Two sprays for weeds and the corn borers. I usually get about 1,150 jin per mu, enough for the family and some to sell.

I do not have cash to throw around on fancy things, so I stick to what has worked before. My neighbors do roughly the same, and if their crops look healthy, I sleep fine. I walk my fields every morning — that is my education.
